purpose: Make the procedural limit memorable: a filed complaint is a question placed before a court, not a verdict.
composition: A bright pop-art editorial still life: four unbranded coloured paper arrows approach a central file folder stamped only with an abstract question mark; the arrows stop at four separate dotted lanes before the folder. A small calendar tab reads September 18 as a visual date cue, with no other text.
mustAvoid: No people, portraits, company logos, product screens, court seals, gavels, scales of justice, judge or jury imagery, factual documentary implication, or generated readable body text.
Never reuse MAiVEN or TRAiLBLAZER portraits.
altText: Pop-art illustration of four unbranded coloured arrows stopping at separate lanes before a question-mark file folder, representing allegations awaiting a legal decision.
admissionNeed: Verify the final image contains no unintended text, logos or documentary implication; bind its exact bytes and independent visual review before article review.
supersessionReason: The arrow-and-question-mark concept was too abstract. The successor binds the final complaint-only story and requires a concrete filed complaint, four separate unbranded subscription receipts and examination without verdict or proven-collusion imagery.
